question:
Let $n\ge1$, and $S=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For a function $f:S\to S$, a subset $D\subset S$ is said to be invariant under $f$, if $f(x)\in D$ for all $x\in D$. Note that the empty set and $S$ are invariant for all $f$. Let $\deg(f)$ be the number of subsets of $S$ invariant under $f$.

(i) Show that there is a function $f:S\to S$ such that $\deg(f)=2$.

(ii) Further show that for any $k$ such that $1\le k\le n$ there is a function $f:S\to S$ such that $\deg(f)=2^k$.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
